harbor_p12_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_001.text: The first field test began in the fourteenth week with three staffed posts on the roster. The office help position would receive longer questions outside the ordinary queue. The mobile route would visit an approved collection point across the inner water. The work-line post would receive concerns from a dry place beside the hauling lane. Yue could take one for her third new-term half-day. Ordinary assigned staff would cover the other two within funded duties. The evening comparison would preserve whose eyes and ears supplied each account instead of turning the visitor's chosen route into the whole town's story.

harbor_p12_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_002.text: Han obtained advance approval for the shared test costs: two copper in forms and copying, six for one bounded interpreter hour at the office, six for the mobile worker's ordinary return ferry. Fourteen would be charged once to the new two-hundred operations allocation, whichever post Yue chose. The remaining posts had their own assigned staff wages already funded. No companion's extra fare was hidden in the six. The public schedule named collection hours and receiving people, with permission questions visible. It looked sensible on the table. Now it had to meet lives that would arrive with their own urgency.

harbor_p12_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_003.text: He Ming read the schedule and noticed the mobile collection point was available only between two tides. A person working that interval might never reach it. The clerk assigned the visit said a written request could be left with the authorized keeper. He Ming asked who could read that request for somebody unable to write. The staff had an answer at the office but none at the far point. Han marked the gap before departure. A concrete question could change the first page before anyone mistook it for completeness.

harbor_p12_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_004.text: Yan moved the work-line post farther from the cart turn after watching an empty cart test. A bench in the first position would narrow the exit. The new dry place could be heard by workers on break and reached without stepping inside a load boundary. He asked the assigned clerk to use spoken instructions rather than invent a bell signal. Bo said people disliked stopping where a foreman could see them reporting. The clerk noted the concern and gave the private intake route. A useful public post also needed a way to speak without an audience pressing around the answer.

harbor_p12_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_005.text: The office help position used an existing table during approved staffed hours, not a new permanent desk created by enthusiasm. Han had another clerk covering her ordinary queue for that interval. The interpreter's hour would support two scheduled questioners who requested it. Anybody else could receive an ordinary explanation and a next appointment where needed. Yue inspected the small sign and liked its honest dates. It promised a task this morning, not a service that would exist whenever somebody remembered the word help and expected a stranger behind the table.

harbor_p12_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_006.text: The mobile worker would travel alone on the six-copper return ticket, carry only permitted requests and keep official pages within the checked-out task packet. Personal addresses would not be displayed on the public collection board. The far keeper had agreed to receive sealed messages under specific permissions for this test, but the office still needed to confirm what happened when a person missed the visit. Han sent that question before the boat left. He Ming watched her write and said the unanswered part should come back with the worker, not remain across the water as a polite assumption.

harbor_p12_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_007.text: Yue listened to the three assignments while holding her own familiar cup. The office could reveal how questions became records. The mobile route could show what happened beyond the window. The work-line post could show the pressure a person carried before asking at all. Each mattered, and each had people who wanted her there for reasons they could explain. Her fourth-stage arms made none of her senses divide into three reliable witnesses. She would choose one half-day and learn the rest through identified accounts, which required accepting that other people would see important things she missed.

harbor_p12_008.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p12_008.text: If you choose the office, I want you to listen where the form stops helping. If you choose another post, I will supply my own signed account of that point instead of pretending you saw it. We do not improve a route by borrowing somebody else's memory as a shared certainty. I am trying to say this without making another morning sound like a hearing. The people coming to us need tea, chairs and an actual answer. The source distinction belongs behind that work, carrying it carefully after we have done it.

harbor_p12_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_009.text: He Ming said the work-line post might receive nothing because fear did not obey a public opening hour. Yan agreed and wanted that result recorded rather than celebrated as proof no worker had concerns. The mobile clerk expected a full list; Han warned the far keeper's availability might change. They were learning to describe a failed attempt before it happened, not as an excuse but as a result someone should examine. Yue felt the assignment become more interesting than the tidy method sheet. The real test would arrive through what people refused, misunderstood, postponed or made impossible without meaning harm.

harbor_p12_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_010.text: A messenger brought the far keeper's reply just before departure. He confirmed the collection interval and could hold sealed replies for later pickup under the stated permission, but had no staff time for open-ended question reading. The office could arrange a separate bounded session if needed. Han attached the reply to the mobile packet. The six-copper fare remained for one worker, not a boatful of advisers improvised at the last moment. Yue was glad the answer came before choice. It made the route limited and honest; the limit itself might be the lesson.

harbor_p12_011.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p12_011.text: Choose where you want to work, Yue. I wanted your presence in every place because I remember what it meant when somebody finally listened. Now I can see that asking the same person everywhere gives the town a new way to avoid assigning anyone else. I will be at my own packing work this morning. Come for supper afterward if you wish. The job can choose a post. Our friendship can choose a table later, when nobody has to call it a duty to make staying pleasant.

harbor_p12_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_012.text: Yue checked the roster and the agreed half-day boundaries. The ordinary staff assigned to the unchosen posts were ready, with specific records and handover routes. She would begin wherever she chose and stop when the scheduled person relieved her. The test's shared costs did not grow because one route felt more dramatic. Its fourteen copper covered the same real operations. She looked from Han's table to the ferry lane and the dry work post beyond it. The harbor had offered three ways to learn where a door failed to open. One morning could enter only one of them firsthand.

choices.text: Listen beside Han at the office help table.
Take the mobile collection route across the inner water.
Receive questions beside Yan's dry work line.

harbor_p12_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_013.text: Yue chose the office help position beside Han Pei. The first questioner was a fish seller named Lu San, who carried a letter asking for contact with an adult son working upriver. He could recognize his son's name but could not write the rest clearly. Han read the existing request form aloud and asked which message he wanted sent. He wanted news, not an address published to relatives. Yue watched the clerk keep that preference visible while helping the man state a usable question. The table felt less like an office once the first cup of tea reached his hands.

harbor_p12_014.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p12_014.text: Your son can answer through this receiving point if he wishes. The request will tell him where your reply can be collected and what you ask. It will not require him to disclose every place he sleeps. If he does not answer, the keeper should return a search status by the stated date, rather than let silence become a claim that he refused. We will give you the receipt and read it with you. You can keep the message personal without making the route depend on remembering my name every time you come back.

harbor_p12_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_015.text: The interpreter's hour helped a second visitor explain a contract phrase he understood as payment delayed until every crew dispute ended. His adviser had meant only the contested part remained under review. Han brought the relevant public explanation and requested the competent adviser's clarification rather than decide the contract herself. Yue heard the man's relief when the distinction became clear, then anger that nobody explained it before. The interpreter preserved both reactions without smoothing the anger into thanks. The visitor accepted a dated referral and asked who would answer if the promised status failed to arrive.

harbor_p12_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_016.text: Han checked the referred desk's roster and found its named responder absent for ordinary care that afternoon. No substitute appeared on the referral note. The contact table could receive the question but had nearly promised an answer by a person unavailable to give it. Yue marked the gap with Han and asked the desk supervisor to identify coverage or correct the deadline. The visitor heard the actual status instead of being sent away under a false certainty. He disliked the delay. A good cup of tea and a clear form had not solved a missing worker behind the next door.

harbor_p12_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_017.text: The supervisor supplied a substitute and a revised specific reply window before the help interval ended. Lu San received his read-back receipt; the contract visitor received the corrected referral and retained his first question date. Yue had observed the office's strength and failure together. Han looked tired, pleased with the correction and annoyed it required discovering the gap in front of someone already waiting. She gave Yue the table report to check for accurate observations. The other posts would send their own accounts. Han did not ask her friend to call the morning successful because its final page was neat.

harbor_p12_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_018.text: When the ordinary relief clerk arrived, Yue handed over the remaining questions and left the table on time. Her own report named what she saw: a readable request helped a man who could not write; interpretation clarified a wage question; a referral nearly outran its assigned responder. Han thanked her for watching the awkward middle instead of only the courteous beginning. Yue understood why the office mattered to her friend in a new way. It could welcome a person sincerely and still fail at the next step unless someone checked whether another living person stood behind the promised answer.

harbor_p12_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_019.text: Yue chose the mobile route and presented the approved return ticket at the ferry. She traveled alone with the checked-out packet, leaving personal household papers at their keepers. The crossing took less than an hour, and the public collection place lay a short safe walk inland. A woman named Rong Qu waited there with a sealed reply she had not known how to return. The authorized keeper had told her when the worker would visit. Yue confirmed her chosen permissions before taking the message into the route, pleased to see a task reach someone who never stood in Han's queue.

harbor_p12_020.speaker: lin_yue
harbor_p12_020.text: I will record that you asked for this reply to travel to the named receiving desk. You keep the receipt, and the office can tell you when it is acknowledged. If you want a different question read or explained, tell me now so I can name the task rather than assume the sealed page contains permission for everything. The keeper's later collection hours are written here. We came to make the route usable for people at this point, not to make you spend a morning proving you should have traveled to the harbor window instead.

harbor_p12_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_021.text: A second visitor arrived after the keeper began his own paid storage work. She wanted a long letter read because she feared it contained a charge against her household. Yue could help within the mobile interval after confirming the permission and relevant scope, but the keeper could not promise the same task every future day. The woman asked what happened if she came next week. Yue supplied the office route for a bounded reading appointment and recorded that no local staffed option existed yet. The mobile visit opened a door once; the next week remained harder.

harbor_p12_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_022.text: Before departure, rain blew across the public board and loosened the lower notice. Rong Qu helped hold it while Yue moved the authorized copy into its dry cover. The keeper objected to more notices taking storage space. He had agreed to sealed collection, not a permanent public office in his own work room. Yue acknowledged the actual agreement and removed an unrelated sheet that arrived without his consent. The woman waiting for reading watched the small negotiation with interest. A useful service could still impose unagreed work on an informal keeper.

harbor_p12_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_023.text: The keeper accepted the agreed packet and signed only the custody he had actually taken. Yue returned on the same permitted ferry ticket, with no extra companion fare charged. Her report identified one successful sealed reply, one missing future reading route, and an unauthorized notice removed from the keeper's space. He Ming would learn the result through its public feedback rather than a claim Yue witnessed every far-bank life. The crossing home was quiet enough to hear rain settle on the canopy. Outreach depended less on the visit than on the person assigned to remain afterward.

harbor_p12_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_024.text: At the landing, Yue returned the checked-out packet and original custody slips to the office keeper. Han read the mobile report and thanked her for preserving the far keeper's limited agreement. The work-line and office staff sent separate signed accounts. Yue knew their results through those sources, not firsthand. She wished it promised more, then remembered Rong Qu's real receipt. The limit did not erase that answer; it named the next task to fund.

harbor_p12_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_025.text: Yue chose the dry work-line post beside the hauling lane. Yan Su showed its ordinary boundary and introduced the relief clerk who would take over after the half-day. For the first hour, nobody brought a question. Workers glanced at the sign and returned to tasks. Bo said the empty page might make the administrator happy. Yue said it should record no questions received in that interval, not prove nobody had any. Yan agreed. The actual test was whether a person could speak without risking the next hiring, and a silent bench supplied no easy answer about that.

harbor_p12_026.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p12_026.text: I can tell workers in my own lane they may call the instructed stop without losing ordinary pay for a safe task. I cannot promise what every hiring foreman in the harbor will do tomorrow. The report desk must receive a specific threat and give a route that survives me taking a day off. If we advertise protection broader than we can carry, silence will look like trust until someone tests it. Stay in this dry place. If a question arrives, listen for the act, the time and what the person wants kept private.

harbor_p12_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_027.text: A porter named Rao Tong finally came during his break and asked whether reporting a stopped load would cost his next shift. A hiring foreman had threatened to deduct time after Rao called the agreed stop over a split strap. Yan's crew confirmed the load stopped under its safety direction. The pay question belonged to the employment route, which could compare contract terms and actual time. Yue received the report with Rao's chosen privacy limits and source contact. She did not promise a criminal verdict or secret immunity. The man wanted an answer he could carry to the next hiring.

harbor_p12_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_028.text: Rao feared the public bench made his visit visible. Yue offered the designated private intake route and asked whether he preferred to move there with the authorized clerk. He did. The brief report received its original date, and the clerk retained the necessary source limits. Outside, another cart approached the turn too quickly. Yan stopped it through ordinary work direction before it reached the post. Yue saw how placement and privacy were both part of the method. A safe bench in the right physical place could still fail the person whose employer watched who sat there.

harbor_p12_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_029.text: The wage adviser received Rao's question through the assigned route and named the contract sources needed. The hiring foreman would be asked to explain the claimed deduction after notice. Yue's account preserved the split-strap stop and the worker's request without publishing his private details on the new sign. Yan looked pleased the post had received something and worried about what followed. He did not call receipt protection completed. The other two posts sent signed reports through their own keepers. Yue had watched one frightened man find a usable beginning, not witnessed a whole harbor learn to speak safely.

harbor_p12_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_030.text: The relief clerk arrived while Rao's follow-up remained active elsewhere. Yue handed over the post record and left within the agreed half-day. Her report named the long empty interval, the visibility concern and the specific stop-pay question. Han later read it alongside office and mobile accounts, each identifying its observer. He Ming asked the public-feedback clerk whether workers who stayed silent had another way to reach the route. The question belonged in the next test. Yue valued having seen the work line because it made the distance between announcing a service and receiving a vulnerable person's words impossible to ignore.

harbor_p12_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_031.text: The three reports met at the office after the field interval. Han identified the office observations; the mobile keeper's slips identified the far route; the work-line clerk identified its report and sources. Yue's signed page named the post she took. The unchosen accounts did not become her memories because they reached her table. Together they showed a helpful beginning, a referral nearly lacking coverage, a mobile visit with no lasting reading staff, and a worker afraid the public bench exposed him. The test had produced actual answers and actual gaps. Neither result erased the other.

harbor_p12_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_032.text: Han entered the shared fourteen-copper cost once: two for forms, six for the interpreter hour, six for the one mobile worker's return ferry. The same charges applied whichever post Yue took. New-term copy authority retained sixteen, interpretation twelve and ferries eighteen. Ordinary staff wages remained in their approved rosters, with no second claim on Yue's fifty-six wage line. The ledger preserved the boring truth beneath three different mornings. The job bought real tasks rather than symbolic choices. He Ming read the public expense summary and said the best part was nobody being thanked into paying a hidden fare.

harbor_p12_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_033.text: The administrator disliked the reports' many unanswered questions. He wanted a clear recommendation for the next fortnight. Han said clarity could include limiting a promise until coverage existed. He Ming wanted the gaps named without making need seem excessive. Yan wanted privacy and physical placement tested together. Yue proposed three specific corrections, each assigned and dated, rather than one new service announced across the town. The administrator asked for costs and available staff time. This was the ordinary pressure under which a small honest report might become a large reassuring fiction if everyone became tired enough to prefer praise.

harbor_p12_034.speaker: lin_yue
harbor_p12_034.text: We can say what worked without making the next person believe every door is staffed. The office gave readable requests and a corrected referral. The far route moved a sealed reply and showed where continuing reading needs a responsible person. The work line received a specific question and showed why a visible bench can deter someone. If we call the whole method successful, we spend the trust of people who arrive tomorrow. I want a smaller statement that lets them know where an actual answer is available, and who must explain when it is not.

harbor_p12_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_035.text: The administrator approved a current substitute list for office referrals, a clearer mobile collection scope, and the work-line private intake route through existing assigned staff. The changes used ordinary office authority and roster time. Any larger continuing local reading service required a separate proposal and allocation, not an assumption Yue's boat ticket created it. Han revised the public schedule under approval. He Ming said she preferred a notice that gave fewer promises honestly. The words surprised her. She now saw how honest limits could prevent another costly search for an unassigned answer.

harbor_p12_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_036.text: Lu San's contact request reached the upriver keeper under its agreed permission. The keeper acknowledged receipt and supplied the expected status date. The old fish seller returned to Han's window only to ask her to read that acknowledgment. A clerk did so when Han was busy. The man left satisfied enough to resume his stall. The route had begun depending on a record other staff could use. Yue liked that result more than being recognized personally at the table. An adult son's reply still belonged to him; the father's question no longer depended on finding one sympathetic woman between shifts.

harbor_p12_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_037.text: The contract visitor received the competent adviser's explanation through the corrected referral. Undisputed payment could proceed while the identified question remained under review. The visitor said he wished the first clerk explained it the same way. The adviser asked which wording caused the confusion and received the old note for comparison. Han's test report supplied the route, not the contract decision. Yue recorded the acknowledgment on her fourth new-term half-day. A useful beginning acquired an actual next step. The next step worked because a responder existed and the visitor knew where to ask.

harbor_p12_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_038.text: Rong Qu's sealed reply reached its receiving desk with the recorded source slip. The office returned acknowledgment through the authorized far keeper. The woman who needed longer reading received a separate bounded appointment after the responsible desk confirmed an available interpreter. That later session belonged to ordinary office resources, not another unapproved charge against the completed test hour. The far keeper retained his agreed collection role and no hidden permanent staff burden. He sent feedback saying the narrower notice was easier to keep. The route improved without turning the inner shore into another wage office.

harbor_p12_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_039.text: Rao Tong's stop-pay question reached the relevant employment reviewer. The foreman received notice and supplied his account and contract term. The stopped load fell within a safety instruction recorded by the ordinary work crew. The reviewer would decide the claimed deduction after comparison, giving Rao a date and route. His privacy preference shaped public status but could not become a promise no respondent ever heard an allegation necessary to answer. The authorized clerk explained that scope before proceeding. Yue did not tell him the mere fact his report arrived meant retaliation was impossible. The test continued beyond opening.

harbor_p12_040.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p12_040.text: The most useful thing we heard was that people still feared the visible post. That does not mean the post should never exist. It means we must offer another actual route and make sure the person staffing it knows the source limits. I want the same instruction to work when I am away fishing or asleep. A foreman who promises safety only while his own voice carries has made the crew dependent on a mood. Put the task in the roster. Then ask a worker whether he can reach it without walking through the person he fears.

harbor_p12_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_041.text: He Ming's second cooperative batch required a later date because one partner had another job. The merchant accepted the available interval and the supported rate. The group bought materials after the agreed advance, hired the same dry space, and paid their own work through the private contract. They did not ask the harbor inquiry to subsidize a slow start. Wu Lian observed the wrapping during a permitted break and asked whether a future small shift might fit her canteen timetable. The cooperative would consider need and availability, not enroll her as gratitude for the rescue story that brought them together.

harbor_p12_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_042.text: An Shou objected to promising Wu a place before the next contract existed. He did not dislike the woman. He feared promising employment because helping felt good. Zhou agreed and suggested teaching a basic method during a clearly private free interval if both chose it, without calling that unpaid production. He Ming accepted. Yue heard the disagreement at supper and admired its difficulty. The partnership's friendships had survived naming limits. It would still need income, tools and honest hours, which no amount of affection for a new arrival could manufacture from the town's feeling of welcome.

harbor_p12_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_043.text: Wu took the offered ordinary method lesson and decided the work might suit occasional hours. She made no production for the merchant during the private session. Her canteen wage remained the family's reliable source. The cooperative needed a future offer before it could buy her time. She thanked He Ming and went home to the inland room, where her children had invented a game involving the toy boat and duck basket. The duck refused the game. Wu said this proved it had read the contract better than anyone else. Her laughter crossed the yard, and the once-annoyed neighbor laughed back.

harbor_p12_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_044.text: Aning and Fen helped the repair shed boy redraw the fish kite's passenger list. He wanted every friend aboard. Fen said the paper would tear if the drawing became too heavy. Aning suggested names in tiny letters along the tail, which nobody could read from the ground. Yue asked whether they needed the list visible or simply wanted it there. They wanted it there. The tail gained a row of private ordinary names that never entered a harbor register. The object could hold memory without pretending it could carry the people named across actual water.

harbor_p12_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_045.text: Luo Jian's next care review permitted more ordinary hand use and still required caution with heavy loading. He decided to extend paper sorting for another month rather than prove recovery by lifting the first bundle offered. Fen looked relieved and tried not to make the relief patronizing. Her father asked whether she would show him the character she practiced last week. She did. He copied it badly and said paper work might be safer if letters had better manners. The joke let them discuss another job without demanding that injury become defeat or entertainment.

harbor_p12_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_046.text: Dai Min bought a better lamp for evening net work from her earned income. She had considered saving every copper until the town's future became certain, then realized certainty was not a purchasable item. The lamp improved a task she actually did. He Ming admired it and asked about its oil cost before proposing the cooperative buy one too. Dai laughed at the practical question. Her husband would have asked about brightness first. She said his memory without crying this time, then grew quiet. Both responses belonged to the evening while the lamp lit thread clearly enough for working hands.

harbor_p12_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_047.text: Miao received an ordinary dispute over one new dispatch wait. His improved term paid the identified waiting period, but the carrier claimed a longer interval than the yard entry showed. They compared the gate record and corrected one late mark. The supported pay went through the merchant's own account. The agent did not need a visitor's approval to do the task properly. Yue saw only the public route feedback when the carrier used the labor advice reference. It showed a change smaller than reforming the harbor and large enough for the person receiving a particular wage this week.

harbor_p12_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_048.text: Han's brush finally made the curve Duan wanted, and the clerk spoiled the next one by anticipating praise. The painter said a successful stroke did not change what the board needed afterward. Han laughed, frustrated but no longer ashamed of the private lesson. She told Yue the mistake over tea. Yue said that sounded like every contact route they tested. Han threatened to charge an interpretation fee for turning painting into office work. They agreed the next half-hour belonged only to bread and a story about Duan's dog, whose habits had no duty to explain any human institution.

harbor_p12_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_049.text: The dog story concerned a stolen glove carried proudly through the painting yard. Duan followed the animal around three boats before discovering it wanted to be paid in food for returning property it took itself. Han said the dog would make a fine merchant agent. Miao, arriving at the stall for supper, overheard and asked whether he should feel accused. She said only if he stole gloves. He laughed awkwardly and bought his own bowl. The group kept its private friendships. They made room for an ordinary shared joke that did not cancel or repeat the commercial hearing.

harbor_p12_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_050.text: The platform accident reviewer sent Deren a current answer about the missing maintenance source. It had been received and required comparison with inspection dates. He remained eligible for the prescribed immediate support already recorded; lost-work findings had the stated next date. Deren thought the process slow and appreciated knowing what had moved. Yan asked whether he wanted help reading the technical page. Deren chose the independent clerk instead, not because their friendship ended but because the question involved Yan's duty. The foreman accepted. Yue saw that reliable friendship could include refusing a friend's help where duty complicated it.

harbor_p12_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_051.text: Sui inspected the emergency shelter roof after ordinary maintenance completed its repair. The keeper tested the formerly leaking corner before restoring those benches to the capacity plan. The plan did not grow merely because a worker said the hole looked closed. Water testing and the building check supplied the result. The reserve's ninety-six shelter-and-care category remained unspent because no activation had occurred. The ordinary repair used its existing maintenance authorization. Yue reviewed only the public updated capacity during her scheduled task, appreciating a dry seat nobody would think to thank while the weather remained kind.

harbor_p12_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_052.text: The weather keeper posted a forecast of strong coastal rain in the coming week, with uncertainty about the tide combination. It was an instrument and observation report, not a prophecy. Sui read the source and asked the harbor master to review mooring, shelter and warning readiness. The six unused emergency stones remained secure, and the fragment screen's rating stayed narrow. Boats and dry routes still carried people. Yue read the public notice after a rest morning and checked whether any contact tasks fell in an unsafe travel interval. A successful mobile visit did not authorize ferries in a worse tide.

harbor_p12_053.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p12_053.text: If the water makes the route unsafe, we postpone it and give the affected people a real status. Do not treat an appointment as a command to travel because the form looks orderly. We have a warning window, a shelter plan and ordinary licensed crews. We also have questions the forecast cannot answer yet. I want the town told what is known before panic invents more. Yue, your field task can help the contact desk keep replies clear. Any separate qi use waits for an agreed safe task and your actual reserve that day.

harbor_p12_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_054.text: Yan checked temporary mooring gear through the work plan. Bo wanted to finish quickly because his family expected him for supper. The foreman showed him the missing check line and offered the authorized shift handover rather than praise his speed. Another worker took the remaining task under the roster. Bo left on time and looked surprised. Deren said this was what happened when adults finally used schedules for their proper purpose. The joke hid a serious pleasure: a person could leave work without making everybody else unsafe or proving that only endless personal sacrifice kept a harbor from falling apart.

harbor_p12_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_055.text: He Ming's partners asked whether the next packing batch should proceed before the forecast rain. They could complete the protected shore work during a safe scheduled interval and store it under the contract's actual dry conditions. If those conditions changed, they would need a new agreement instead of moving parcels into an unapproved shed. He Ming wrote the weather limit plainly. The merchant accepted because spoiled wrapping would help no one. Wu did not take a paid production shift yet. The partnership had no real demand for another worker yet, and said so clearly.

harbor_p12_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_056.text: Han paid Yue eight copper for the first four completed half-days of the new term. The first two weeks' agreed bed and meals came to twelve, paid through the new eighty-four line after the keeper's invoice check. Shared test expenses were fourteen: copies two, interpretation six, ferry six. Thirty-four of the two hundred had therefore been spent, leaving one hundred sixty-six within its separate purposes. Remaining wages were forty-eight, bed and meals seventy-two, ferry eighteen, copies sixteen and interpretation twelve. The initial forty-four unspent remained closed under operations control and was not silently added to this balance.

harbor_p12_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_057.text: The separate emergency reserve still stood at sixteen spent and two hundred twenty-four unspent. Eight stones had been purchased, two exhausted in drill and six unused held for rated tasks. Extra-shift, shelter-and-care, and message-boat categories had not yet been activated or charged. The report distinguished physical stock from cash. Yue's personal reserve had recovered through rest and remained fourth-stage. Nobody treated her new wage as fuel or counted the wrapped pendant among emergency stores. The account sat behind the town's readiness, leaving the foreground to people securing shutters, checking ropes and deciding where relatives would wait if rain became severe.

harbor_p12_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_058.text: Wu closed her room's shutters with help from the neighbor whose sleep the duck once interrupted. He showed the latch he repaired before her arrival and asked her children not to swing it for amusement. They agreed with all the solemnity children use before testing a rule later. He Ming carried a parcel of food as a private purchase Wu asked her to make. Yue joined supper by invitation and walked home before the rain. The family had a farther bed and nearby people willing to share practical work. The imperfect workable room mattered more than the office label settled.

harbor_p12_059.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_059.text: Fen moved the kite indoors and told the boy no amount of legal argument would make wet paper enjoy a storm. He blamed the sea's appeal. Aning brought a strip of dry cloth for its storage wrap with the owner's permission to give it. Luo checked the hook without using his injured hand for heavy work. The object remained safe through ordinary attention. Yue touched its named tail and felt how many people had become part of a place she once entered alone. The term did not buy friendships. It gave her time among them while the town changed.

harbor_p12_060.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_060.text: Han walked with Yue to the shore wall at dusk. The forecast cloud lay low beyond the channel, soft enough to look harmless from a dry street. They spoke about the field test's unfinished reading route and then stopped discussing work. Han asked whether Yue feared the coming weather. She said yes, especially for people she now knew. The clerk admitted the same. Neither pretended careful records removed fear. They prepared actual tasks and shared an ordinary evening. When rain reached the wall, both went home.

harbor_p12_061.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_061.text: The fifteenth week's preliminary roster named extra crews only within the authorized emergency categories if activation occurred. The harbor master would decide safe transport; Sui would handle relevant technical tasks; Yan would manage assigned rigging; ordinary care staff would receive injured people. Contact work had its named desk and handover. Yue would take her scheduled part and any separately agreed small task she could actually do. The roster supplied no secret higher rank. It was the harbor's answer to the weather while uncertainty remained, a plan made from fallible people who knew enough to ask one another what they needed.

harbor_p12_062.speaker: narrator
harbor_p12_062.text: Yue ended the fourteenth week with her personal notes open beside the familiar cup. She recorded the three field accounts separately, the actual thirty-four spent from her new term, and the test's limits. Those official facts would remain at their keepers; her notes held what she learned. Her qi practice still showed two earned pairs and measured rest. Outside, someone called the tide reading through the darkening lane, and another voice repeated it. The sound began a story she could not finish in advance. She closed her notes and slept before the next morning.
